fields.description: A foundational lower-body exercise that trains the legs and glutes using body weight.
fields.instructions: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart. Push your hips back and bend your knees. Lower with control while keeping your chest lifted. Push through your feet to return to standing.
fields.common_mistakes: Knees collapsing inward, heels lifting, rounding the back, and dropping too quickly.
fields.safety_tips: Keep the movement controlled and use a comfortable depth. Stop if you feel sharp pain.

fields.description: A unilateral lower-body exercise that develops leg strength, balance, and stability.
fields.instructions: Stand tall and step one foot backward. Lower your body until both knees are comfortably bent. Push through the front foot to return to standing and alternate sides.
fields.common_mistakes: Front knee collapsing inward, taking an unstable step, and leaning excessively forward.
fields.safety_tips: Use a wall or stable support if balance is limited.

fields.description: A floor-based exercise focused on glute activation and hip extension.
fields.instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips. Pause briefly and lower with control.
fields.common_mistakes: Overarching the lower back, pushing mainly through the toes, and moving too quickly.
fields.safety_tips: Keep the ribs controlled and stop if the movement causes back pain.

fields.description: A simple exercise for strengthening the calf muscles and ankle control.
fields.instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Rise onto the balls of your feet, pause at the top, then slowly lower your heels.
fields.common_mistakes: Bouncing, rolling the ankles outward, and using momentum.
fields.safety_tips: Hold a stable surface if needed for balance.

fields.description: An isometric lower-body exercise that builds leg endurance.
fields.instructions: Place your back against a wall and slide down until your knees are comfortably bent. Hold the position while keeping your back supported.
fields.common_mistakes: Knees moving far inward, sliding too low too soon, and holding the breath.
fields.safety_tips: Choose a comfortable knee angle and stop if you experience joint pain.

fields.description: A bodyweight upper-body exercise for chest, shoulders, triceps, and core.
fields.instructions: Start in a plank position with hands slightly wider than the shoulders. Bend the elbows to lower the chest, then push the floor away to return.
fields.common_mistakes: Sagging hips, flared elbows, and moving the head instead of the body.
fields.safety_tips: Use an incline or knee variation if a full push-up is too difficult.

fields.description: A beginner-friendly push-up variation using an elevated surface.
fields.instructions: Place your hands on a stable elevated surface. Keep your body in a straight line, lower your chest toward the surface, and push back.
fields.common_mistakes: Bending at the hips, unstable surface, and flaring the elbows.
fields.safety_tips: Use only a stable, non-slippery surface.

fields.description: An upper-body resistance exercise for shoulder strength.
fields.instructions: Hold dumbbells at shoulder height. Brace your core and press the weights overhead without leaning backward. Lower them with control.
fields.common_mistakes: Using excessive weight, arching the lower back, and pressing unevenly.
fields.safety_tips: Use a manageable weight and keep the movement pain-free.

fields.description: A resistance exercise that targets the elbow flexors.
fields.instructions: Stand tall holding dumbbells with palms facing forward. Bend the elbows to curl the weights toward the shoulders, then lower slowly.
fields.common_mistakes: Swinging the body, moving the elbows excessively, and dropping the weights quickly.
fields.safety_tips: Use a weight that allows controlled repetitions.

fields.description: A pulling exercise that develops the upper back and arm muscles.
fields.instructions: Hinge forward with a neutral back while holding dumbbells. Pull the weights toward your ribs, squeeze the shoulder blades, then lower them.
fields.common_mistakes: Rounding the back, shrugging the shoulders, and using momentum.
fields.safety_tips: Maintain a comfortable neutral spine and use an appropriate weight.

fields.description: An isometric core exercise that develops trunk stability.
fields.instructions: Start on your forearms and toes with your body in a straight line. Brace your core and hold without letting the hips sag or rise excessively.
fields.common_mistakes: Dropping the hips, lifting the hips too high, and holding the breath.
fields.safety_tips: Reduce the duration or use knees as support if needed.

fields.description: A controlled core and balance exercise that trains opposite arm and leg coordination.
fields.instructions: Start on hands and knees. Extend one arm and the opposite leg while keeping the trunk stable. Pause, return, and alternate sides.
fields.common_mistakes: Rotating the hips, arching the back, and moving too quickly.
fields.safety_tips: Keep the range of motion comfortable and controlled.

fields.description: A core stability exercise that teaches controlled limb movement while maintaining trunk position.
fields.instructions: Lie on your back with arms up and knees bent. Brace your core and slowly extend the opposite arm and leg. Return and alternate sides.
fields.common_mistakes: Lower back lifting from the floor, moving too quickly, and losing core tension.
fields.safety_tips: Use a smaller range of motion if maintaining the position is difficult.

fields.description: A dynamic bodyweight exercise combining core stability with cardiovascular conditioning.
fields.instructions: Start in a high plank. Drive one knee toward the chest, return it, then switch sides in a controlled rhythm.
fields.common_mistakes: Bouncing the hips excessively, losing plank alignment, and moving beyond control.
fields.safety_tips: Slow the pace for beginners and stop if you feel pain or dizziness.

fields.description: A simple full-body cardio exercise for warm-ups and conditioning.
fields.instructions: Stand tall with feet together. Jump while moving the feet apart and arms overhead, then return to the starting position.
fields.common_mistakes: Landing stiffly, poor coordination, and excessive speed.
fields.safety_tips: Use a low-impact step-out version if jumping is uncomfortable.

fields.description: A cardio drill that raises the heart rate and trains coordinated leg movement.
fields.instructions: Stand tall and alternate lifting the knees toward hip height while maintaining an upright posture. Move at a controlled pace.
fields.common_mistakes: Leaning backward, landing heavily, and losing control of the knees.
fields.safety_tips: March instead of running if impact is uncomfortable.

fields.description: A controlled hip-extension exercise that targets the glutes.
fields.instructions: Start on hands and knees. Keeping the knee bent, lift one foot upward by squeezing the glute. Lower slowly and switch sides.
fields.common_mistakes: Rotating the pelvis, arching the lower back, and using momentum.
fields.safety_tips: Keep the movement small enough to maintain a stable spine.

fields.description: A balance and hip-strengthening exercise for the muscles on the outside of the hip.
fields.instructions: Stand tall while holding a stable support if needed. Move one leg out to the side without leaning the torso, then return slowly.
fields.common_mistakes: Leaning the torso, rotating the foot outward, and swinging the leg.
fields.safety_tips: Use a stable support and keep the movement controlled.

fields.description: A gentle spinal mobility exercise that moves the spine through flexion and extension.
fields.instructions: Start on hands and knees. Slowly round the spine while looking toward the body, then gently extend the spine while lifting the chest.
fields.common_mistakes: Moving too quickly, forcing the range, and straining the neck.
fields.safety_tips: Move gently within a comfortable range and stop if symptoms worsen.

fields.description: A simple shoulder mobility exercise suitable for warm-ups.
fields.instructions: Stand tall and extend the arms out to the sides. Make small controlled circles, gradually increasing the circle size as comfortable.
fields.common_mistakes: Using fast uncontrolled circles and shrugging the shoulders.
fields.safety_tips: Keep the circles pain-free and reduce the range if needed.

fields.description: A gentle flexibility exercise for the back of the thigh.
fields.instructions: Extend one leg comfortably and hinge forward slightly from the hips while keeping the back relaxed. Hold the stretch without bouncing, then switch sides.
fields.common_mistakes: Bouncing, forcing the stretch, and rounding aggressively through the back.
fields.safety_tips: Stretch to mild tension rather than pain or numbness.

fields.description: A standing flexibility exercise for the front of the thigh.
fields.instructions: Stand tall and hold a stable support if needed. Bend one knee and bring the heel toward the glutes while keeping the knees close. Hold and switch sides.
fields.common_mistakes: Pulling aggressively, arching the back, and allowing the knee to move far forward.
fields.safety_tips: Use support for balance and avoid forcing the knee.

fields.description: A gentle mobility and relaxation position commonly used for recovery and flexibility.
fields.instructions: Kneel comfortably and sit the hips back toward the heels. Reach the arms forward and breathe slowly while maintaining a comfortable position.
fields.common_mistakes: Forcing the hips downward, holding the breath, and pushing through pain.
fields.safety_tips: Use a cushion or reduce the range if the knees or hips are uncomfortable.

fields.description: A balance exercise that develops lower-limb stability and body control.
fields.instructions: Stand near a stable support. Lift one foot slightly from the floor and maintain an upright posture. Hold, lower the foot, and switch sides.
fields.common_mistakes: Looking down constantly, locking the standing knee, and moving away from support too soon.
fields.safety_tips: Perform beside a stable surface and progress gradually.

fields.description: A very beginner-friendly upper-body pushing exercise performed against a wall.
fields.instructions: Stand facing a wall with hands at shoulder height. Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall, then push away to return.
fields.common_mistakes: Leaning from the hips, placing hands too high, and moving too quickly.
fields.safety_tips: Use a stable wall and maintain a comfortable range of motion.
